critical_evidence.evidence: The seller discloses track and autocross use himself: autocross 2-3 times per year and several HPDE sessions. He says oil is checked before events and the engine 'has never burned oil.' No measured oil-consumption data is provided, and no compression or leakdown test has been done. Both are needed at the PPI because the car has been tracked.

The listing and seller state the car is stock apart from the brake pads. The exterior photos show stock-appearing exhaust tips. No ECU scan or engine-bay inspection has confirmed there is no tune or headers; the engine bay was not examined here.
NHTSA 18V772000 covers 2013 cars; this is a 2016, VIN-confirmed.

NHTSA 21V587000 covers 2018-2019 cars; this is a 2016, and the tracker shows no open recalls for this VIN. The seller separately reports a 2018 warranty fuel-pump replacement for chirping, which is a service bulletin item.

documentation.rationale: Identity and terms are present: VIN decode match, clean VA title stated, platform-noted clean Carfax, one owner since new, reserve disclosed. The maintenance side is partial. One dated service (May 2024) is documented in the gallery, and records are included, but the full history, coolant service and Carfax were not examined here.

condition.rationale: Positives rest on unverified or partial evidence: no leaks claimed, new rotors in June 2026, tires from 2022, photos showing straight panels and intact factory wheels. Against that, the car has disclosed underbody corrosion of unknown extent, track and autocross use on the original clutch, chips and dings, upholstery wear, and a repainted spoiler.

price_value.rationale: There is no fair-value estimate. Comps put stock, lower-mile BRZs at about $16.4k–$17k, and this car's tracked history and corrosion should place it below them. The current $6,500 bid means nothing against an unknown reserve. The value is plausible if it hammers within the ideal band, with no firm known-work deductions.

mission_fit.rationale: It is a stock, naturally aspirated, manual first-gen BRZ, a named secondary bridge candidate. It should be reliable, cheap to run and easy to resell, and expected pricing sits inside the $10k–$19k ideal band. The track history and remote auction format temper that.

logistics.rationale: The car is in Warrenton, VA, across the country from Carmel, and closes in about three days as a reserve auction. PPI access is unstated, though the seller is very cooperative and local shops are plentiful. A stock car should make CA smog and registration straightforward.

emotional_spec_fit.rationale: It combines WR Blue, the Limited trim, a 6-speed manual, one owner and a largely unmodified spec, which is increasingly rare for a first-gen twin. Enthusiast track use and cosmetic wear keep it below the top band.

positives: Stock first-gen BRZ with a factory 6-speed manual, WR Blue, Limited trim. The VIN decode matches, and the seller claims one owner since June 2016 on a clean VA title.

Service documentation is shown in the gallery for May 2024 at 55,214 mi: spark plugs, brake fluid, transmission and differential fluid, oil, filters and alignment. Mostly dealer maintenance is claimed.
The seller volunteered unflattering facts himself: track and autocross use, underbody corrosion, a repainted spoiler, and cosmetic and upholstery flaws.
The odometer photo (58,717) corroborates the listed mileage. Photos show straight panels, factory wheels with no visible damage and an intact stock interior.
Consumables are fairly recent: new OEM rotors in June 2026 and Continental tires installed June 2022 with about 7,000 miles on them.
The seller is highly engaged: extra underbody and engine-bay media, detailed answers, and in-person viewing offered.
concerns: Observed: disclosed autocross (2-3 times per year) and several HPDE track days. The clutch is original, and the FA20 is known for oiling sensitivity under sustained high-g, so compression, leakdown and clutch health are open.

Observed: disclosed corrosion on underbody components after years in FL, OR and VA. A commenter saw suspension parts starting to look 'crunchy'; the extent on subframes, control arms and brake/fuel lines is not examined here.

Unverified: coolant replacement and any service outside the May 2024 visit (ask for the full dealer records and the Carfax).

ppi_focus: Underbody corrosion survey: subframes, control arms, sway-bar links, brake and fuel hard lines, exhaust hangers, pinch welds and jacking points
Compression and leakdown test, plus oil condition, to address the disclosed track use
Clutch slip test in high gear, release point, throwout-bearing noise and clutch hydraulics on the original clutch
OBD scan for stored and pending codes and readiness monitors; identify the lit amber indicator; check the ECU for any flash history
Oil seepage at the timing cover, cam plugs and valve covers; check coolant age and condition
Brakes: DTC-30 pad and rotor condition, brake fluid moisture and boiling point, caliper condition
Paint-meter readings on all panels to confirm only the spoiler was repainted and no undisclosed accident repair exists
Tire DOT dates and wear pattern for alignment or hard-use clues; check the rear differential for leaks and noise
what_would_change_verdict: Up: the PPI shows even compression and leakdown, surface-only corrosion and a healthy clutch, and a clean scan identifies the amber lamp as benign
Up: full dealer records and the Carfax confirm continuous service, including coolant, and the one-owner, no-accident history
Down: corrosion on brake or fuel lines, subframes or suspension mounts that needs replacement, or poor leakdown or oil consumption from track use
Down: the seller cannot or will not allow a PPI before close, or the amber lamp is a stored engine or VSC fault
evidence.mission_note: A stock, naturally aspirated manual BRZ squarely fits the enthusiast-bridge brief: simple, cheap to run, engaging, and easy to resell within 6-24 months. Accelerated-bridge mode still means no bidding blind on a tracked, corrosion-disclosed car without an inspection.
evidence.rationale: The listing establishes a VIN-matched 2016 BRZ Limited with a factory 6-speed manual, an odometer photo at 58,717 consistent with the stated mileage, a claimed clean VA title and one-owner history, and a platform-noted May 2024 service covering plugs and all major fluids. Observed issues come from the seller's own disclosures: autocross and several HPDE days on the original clutch, corrosion on some underbody components after years in FL, OR and VA, track-compound brake pads, a repainted spoiler, chips and dings, and upholstery wear visible in the rear-seat photo. An unidentified amber indicator is lit in the engine-running cluster photo. The model-critical track item is disclosed but backed only by seller statements, with no compression, leakdown or measured oil consumption. Tune status is claimed stock, and both recall items are not applicable to a 2016. Comps suggest a hammer in the low-to-mid teens given the track history and corrosion, but the reserve is unknown. PPI access before the Monday close has not been addressed.
